key_insight: This paper shows that LLM agents can help automate two costly parts of science: reproducing published results and checking whether findings stay stable under reasonable analytical changes. Using a medical case study, the authors introduce a benchmark to test how well AI can support reproducibility and robustness analysis.
problem_solved: Scientific studies are often difficult to reproduce and validate manually, especially when they depend on complex datasets and many analytical choices. This paper tackles the high cost and effort of verifying whether published findings are both reproducible and analytically robust.
method: Built SEER-Repro, a benchmark based on 20 published studies using the SEER cancer registry.
Evaluated whether LLM agents can reproduce study results from the original papers and underlying data.
Tested AI-assisted robustness analysis by examining how findings change under alternative analytical decisions.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work points to a practical use of LLM agents beyond generation: supporting scientific validation. It suggests a path toward faster, cheaper checks of reproducibility and robustness in data-driven research.

paper_title: AI-Driven Reproducibility and Analytical Robustness in Scientific Discovery
paper_authors: Shicheng Liu, Krista Opsahl-Ong, Andrew Drozdov, Julian Killingback, Arnav Singhvi
